mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which is associated with lower earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months after a prior contraction signals a supply-side recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5% q/q).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo avg for 2 consecutive months after 2 months below, AND CPIAUCSL <= 5% q/q
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes with CPIAUCSL <= 5% q/q.
